name: Lactoferrin supplement

lead: Lactoferrin is a protein found in milk (highest in colostrum), saliva and tears, commercially purified from bovine milk or made by fermentation. It binds iron and has antimicrobial and immune-modulating activity.
Users take it for immune support and lower inflammation, which feeds into recovery and training consistency, and some for skin-related goals.

paras: Taken as an oral capsule or powder, alone or with probiotics or iron. Studies run for weeks.
Evidence for medicinal use is limited and bioavailability not well understood; supplements are not regulated like drugs, so quality may vary.

angle.text: Users take it to support immune function and manage inflammation, which they connect to training consistency and physique progress.

lead: Lactoferrin is a globular glycoprotein of the transferrin family that binds iron and is found in milk, mucus and neutrophils. Commercial supplements use bovine milk or recombinant sources.[1][2]

A 2022 meta-analysis of 25 studies found lactoferrin reduced IL-6 in adults and some trials showed fewer respiratory infections.[3] People link lower inflammation and fewer illnesses to steadier training and recovery.

paras: Its main role is binding and transporting iron, limiting iron available to bacteria; antimicrobial and immune effects are described in lab studies.[1]

A 2022 systematic review of 25 studies found decreased inflammatory biomarkers in 8 of 13 adult studies and reduced respiratory infection outcomes in 6 of 10 studies; IL-6 fell but not CRP.[3] Wikipedia notes low-quality evidence in preterm infants for late-onset sepsis.[1] A trial in children with inflammatory bowel disease examined lactoferrin for iron-deficiency anemia.[4]
Quality evidence for medicinal use is limited, bioavailability is not well understood, and supplements lack medicine-level regulation.[1]

timeline.event: China approves recombinant bovine lactoferrin made by precision fermentation.[1]
